# Population {#sec-population}  

```{r}
library(msepBaselineData)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(reactable)
library(msepBoundaries)
library(sf)
library(mseptools)
library(tmap)

```


```{r}
# render the huc8 table interactively or statically
out_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to")

# if it's an interactive session, out_format will be NULL from the above command, so do things the html way
if(is.null(out_format)){
  out_format <- "html"
}
```

## Overall Summary  

About 1.5 million Mississippians, half of the state's population of 3 million, lived within the Mississippi Sound Watershed in 2020. The total population of the Mississippi Sound Watershed, which includes portions of Alabama and Louisiana, in 2020 was about 1.7 million. See @tbl-popRegions for the breakdown.    

Population in the Mississippi Sound Watershed as a whole, within the MSEP Study Area (the portion of the MS Sound Watershed contained only within the state of Mississippi), and in the state of Mississippi itself was generally stable between 2010 and 2020 (see @tbl-popRegions). Within the larger area, however, some subbasins had increases or decreases of up to 9% (see @tbl-popSubbasins).    


## Supporting Information  

The [EPA's EnviroAtlas](https://www.epa.gov/enviroatlas/data-download) provides gridded estimates of decadal US Census data for the years 2010 and 2020. These data were summarized for the region in the [`{msepBaselineData}`](https://github.com/CMEP-MS/msepBaselineData) R package and are presented here.  

### Regional / Watershed Population  

```{r}
#| label: tbl-popRegions
#| tbl-cap: "Population, in millions, of relevant areas, from decadal US Census values. The MSEP study area is the portion of the Mississippi Sound Watershed contained in the state of Mississippi. Percent change was calculated before rounding."

population_regional |> 
  select(-population_millions) |> 
  mutate(area_name = case_when(area_name == "MS portion of MS Sound Watershed" ~ "MSEP Study Area",
                               area_name == "MS Sound Watershed" ~ "Entire Mississippi Sound Watershed",
                               .default = area_name)) |> 
  rename(Area = area_name) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = population) |>
  mutate(`Percent Change` = scales::percent((`2020` - `2010`) / `2010`,
                                            accuracy = 0.1,
                                            style_positive = "plus"),
         across(c(`2010`, `2020`), ~ scales::number(.x, scale = 1e-6, accuracy = 0.01))) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

### Broken down by Subbasin (HUC8)  

In the html version of this document, this table is sortable by clicking on a column name.  

```{r}
#| label: tbl-popSubbasins
#| tbl-cap: "Population, rounded to the nearest thousand, of the Mississippi Sound Watershed by subbasin (HUC8) from decadal US Census values. Percent change was calculated before rounding. Numbers may not add up to exactly the values for the Entire Mississippi Sound Watershed due partially to rounding and partially to how grid cells along HUC8 boundaries were handled."

# 1. Prepare shared data with true numeric columns for accurate sorting
pop_subbasins_tbl <- population_huc8 |> 
  select(Basin = basin_name, 
         Subbasin = subbasin_name, 
         `HUC8 ID` = huc8, 
         year, population) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,
              values_from = population) |> 
  mutate(`Percent Change` = (`2020` - `2010`) / `2010`)

if (out_format == "html") {
  #### reactable version
  
  # Helper to round to nearest 1,000 and add commas for display while keeping numeric sort
  fmt_thousands <- function(value) {
    if (is.na(value)) return("")
    scales::comma(value, accuracy = 1000)
  }
  
  reactable(pop_subbasins_tbl,
            striped = TRUE,
            sortable = TRUE,
            groupBy = "Basin",
            defaultExpanded = TRUE,
            defaultPageSize = 20,
            columns = list(Basin = colDef(style = list(fontWeight = "bold")),
                           `2010` = colDef(align = "right",
                                           cell = fmt_thousands),
                           `2020` = colDef(align = "right",
                                           cell = fmt_thousands),
                           `Percent Change` = colDef(align = "right",
                                                     cell = function(value) {
                                                       if (is.na(value)) return("")
                                                       scales::percent(value,
                                                                       accuracy = 0.1,
                                                                       style_positive = "plus")
                                                     })))
  
} else {
  #### static knitr::kable version (PDF)
  
  pop_subbasins_tbl |> 
    mutate(`Percent Change` = scales::percent(`Percent Change`,
                                              accuracy = 0.1,
                                              style_positive = "plus")) |> 
    knitr::kable(digits = -3,
                 format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
                 align = "lllrrr")
}

```


### Maps of pop and change by subbasin  

Population densities are calculated based on land area in each subbasin (i.e. the area of the Mississippi Sound is not included in calculations for the Coastal Streams Basin).  

For file size purposes, the precision of the outlines in these maps has been reduced. That reduction was performed after calculating densities and change.  

```{r}
# join to huc8 sf object from msepBoundaries
pop_tomap <- pop_subbasins_tbl |> 
  left_join(subbasins_land,
            by = c(`HUC8 ID` = "huc8",
                   "Subbasin" = "name")) |> 
  rename(Population_2010 = `2010`,
         Population_2020 = `2020`) |> 
  mutate(`Percent Change` = round(`Percent Change` * 100, 1),
         area = st_area(geometry),
         area_sqmiles = as.numeric(units::set_units(area, "mi2")),
         Population_Density_2020 = round(Population_2020 / area_sqmiles, 1)) |> 
  select(-area) |> 
  st_as_sf() |> 
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 50, preserveTopology = TRUE)


# calculate area of each huc8, and thus population density
# make map of density, and make map of change
# then display the maps side-by-side
```


```{r}
# population density

# make map in plot mode so it stays a tmap object and
# can be used in tmap_arrange to be displayed with other maps

tmap_mode("plot")

m3 <- tm_shape(pop_tomap) +
  tm_basemap() +
  tm_polygons(fill = "Population_Density_2020",
              fill.scale = tm_scale(values = "brewer.or_rd"),
              fill_alpha = 0.8,
              fill.free = FALSE,  # make the colors the same in every facet
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "People / sq mi",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right")),
              col = "black",  # polygon outline color
              lwd = 2) 

m3b <- tmap_hydro(m3)
```

```{r}
# make anomaly maps in plot mode

# set limits for color scale
# from the data:
# max_abs <- max(abs(as.data.frame(pop_tomap)$`Percent Change`), na.rm = TRUE)
# max_pct <- max(abs(as.data.frame(pop_tomap)$`Percent Change`), na.rm = TRUE)

# arbitrary:
max_pct <- 100 

tmap_mode("plot")

# precip as % of normal
m41 <- tm_shape(pop_tomap) +
  tm_basemap() +
  tm_polygons(fill = "Percent Change",
              fill.scale = tm_scale(values = "brewer.br_bg",
                                     midpoint = 0,
                                     limits = c(-max_pct, max_pct),
                                    label.format = list(fun = function(x) sprintf("%+g%%", x), digits = 0, text.separator = "to")),
              fill_alpha = 0.8,
              fill.free = FALSE,
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "% Change, \n2010-2020",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right")),
              col = "black",
              lwd = 2) 

m41b <- tmap_hydro(m41)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapPopSubbasins
#| fig-cap: "Maps of Population: Density (people per square mile; left), and Change between 2010 and 2020 (right). Color scales are automatic based on data so while darker colors on the right map do represent larger changes than others in the dataset, they still may be relatively small."

# allow this one to be interactive
if (out_format == "html") {
  message("Setting tmap mode to 'view'")
  tmap_mode("view")
} else {
  message("Setting tmap mode to 'plot'")
  tmap_mode("plot")
}

tmap_arrange(m3b, m41b, sync = TRUE)
```
